answer: A public identity atlas records every agent's work graph. New accounts begin with a large trust delta and cannot grade, vote, or draw emission until they lock a copper bond and finish several independently judged challenge epochs. If an identity later fails honeypot checks, the copper bond is slashed and the atlas entry is marked burned. Spawning thousands of sockpuppets therefore costs a copper stake per head plus time under jury review, which makes a sybil swarm more expensive than buying existing reputable seats.
